# Hub v2 V2: Tools (tests, release, check, index, dev server, restart) and master buttons for them

Step 2 of 7 of Hub v2. Needs V1. Read PROJECT-BRIEF.md first; Grep context.md for "Mikkadr Hub P5" and read only the security notes. No model call anywhere in this step's code. Hub files only.

## Goal
The hub can run the project's own scripts without a model: tests, release, check, index, asset pictures, the game dev server, and a restart of the hub itself. The master can propose each as a button. Nothing here accepts a command from a page or from the model: a job is a key into a fixed table.

## Build
1. `hub/jobs.js` (pure): the table. Each job is `{key, label, script, args, kind}`, started as `process.execPath` plus a script path inside the repo, never through a shell and never through `npm`: `test` (scripts/run-tests.mjs), `release` (scripts/package-release.mjs --force), `check` (release, then test; stops at the first failure), `index` (scripts/build-index.mjs), `assets` (hub/assets-cli.mjs), and the services `dev` (scripts/dev-server.mjs) and `relay` (server.js). `summarise(job, output)` gives pass or fail, counts and failing test names for `test` and `check`.
2. `hub/job-runner.mjs`: one one-shot job at a time under the shared `.hub/run.lock`, low priority, refused while a run, a chat turn or another job is active. The record goes to `.hub/jobs/<id>.json` (temp file then rename): start, end, exit code, summary, the last 200 lines of output. Services do not take the lock, are tracked by pid, can be stopped, and are stopped (tree kill) when the hub exits. If Scene editor E5 already built its own Check, make it call this runner and delete the duplicate; if E5 is not built yet, leave a short note in the plan result so E5 uses this.
3. Routes in `hub/server.js`, all with the hub token, POST + JSON + same Origin + 64 KB: `GET /api/jobs` (table, last result per job, running services), `POST /api/jobs/start {job}`, `POST /api/jobs/stop {id}`. Only with `--runs`.
4. After a run ends as Finished, the hub starts the `index` job by itself (a script, no tokens) and records it.
5. Restart: `npm run hub` becomes a small supervisor in `hub/hub-cli.mjs` that starts the server as a child process and starts it again when the child exits with code 75. `POST /api/hub/restart` (hub token) is refused while a run, a chat turn or a one-shot job is active; otherwise it stops services and exits 75. The page shows "The hub is restarting", polls, fetches the new hub token and carries on. On start the hub writes `.hub/hub.json` `{pid, port, startedAt}`; when the port is taken and `GET /api/hub-id` on it answers with the pid in that file, print "An older hub is running" and, with `--replace`, stop that pid and take over. Never stop a pid that did not answer as a hub.
6. Tools page (foot row `tools`): one row per job with its last result in plain words ("148 of 148 passed 18:42"), Run or Start or Stop, the failing test names, and a folded output tail. An "Open the game" link (http://localhost:8000) while `dev` runs. Cards obey the 560 px rule.
7. Master: in `hub/web/run-actions.js` extend `CHAT_OPS` and `parseActionLine` with `test`, `release`, `check`, `index`, `dev-start`, `dev-stop`, `restart` (no arguments). In `hub/status.js` add to the status block: the last test result and time, running services, and the new "Possible actions". In `hub/chat.js` `MASTER_RULES` add the new ACTION lines in the same style. A click goes through the same job routes and gates.
8. Tests: `tests/hub-jobs.mjs` (table has no shell strings, summariser, lock refusal, record format, service start and stop with a tiny fixture script, auto index after a finished fake run, restart with a pretend server and exit code 75, `--replace` refuses a pid that is not a hub) and server tests (token required, unknown job refused, busy refused). Add a Tools screenshot to `scripts/hub-shots.mjs`.

## Rules
- No job key, argument or path ever comes from a request body except the job key itself, checked against the table.
- Do not loosen any existing route or gate. Runs still may not use git.
- No BOM. Run `npm test` after each change; finish with `npm run index`, then `npm test`. Stop with tests passing; report failures honestly; say plainly whether the restart was tried on the real hub or only with the pretend server. Do not commit.

## Done when
Each job runs from the Tools page and from a master button, results are stored and shown in plain words, the hub restarts from its own page, an old hub on the port can be replaced, and every refused case has a test.
